title: The High Street
dek: A high street with shops below and flats above, a zebra crossing, a café and a bus stop.
frames: The … is next to / between / opposite the …
Go past the … and turn left.
Excuse me, is there a … near here?
I need to go to the … to …

truefalse.s: There is a red car on the road.
The café is next to the bank.
There are three people at the bus stop.
The cyclist is wearing a helmet.
The bookshop is between the café and the clothes shop.
The post box is outside the bakery.
You can get money from the cash machine at the bank.
Someone is crossing the road at the zebra crossing.
The chemist's has a green cross on its sign.
There are two mannequins in the window of the clothes shop.
The menu board is outside the bookshop.
The bus shelter has a timetable in it.
There are flats above the shops.
The lamp post is in front of the post office.
Someone is holding an umbrella outside the clothes shop.

A1: What shops are there on your street?
Look at the picture. What can you buy in each shop?
Write five sentences with next to and between.
A2: Give directions from the bus stop to the post office.
Plan a Saturday morning on this high street: where do you go and why?
Describe the high street in your town. What's good? What's missing?
B1: Are high street shops dying because of online shopping? Give your view.
Write a review of the café for a local website.
What would make this street better for pedestrians and cyclists?

rooms.ex: There's a new café on the high street.
rooms.def: The main street of a town, with most of the shops.

rooms.ex: I buy fresh bread from the bakery every morning.
rooms.def: A shop that makes and sells bread and cakes.

rooms.ex: Can you get me some plasters at the chemist's?
rooms.def: A shop that sells medicine, soap and make-up.

rooms.ex: I need to post this parcel at the post office.
rooms.def: The place where you send letters and parcels.
A place that keeps your money safe.

rooms.ex: Let's meet at the café for a coffee.
rooms.def: A small restaurant for drinks and light meals.

rooms.ex: The bookshop has a sale this week.
I bought this jacket in the clothes shop.
Wait for me at the bus stop.
rooms.def: A place where the bus stops for people to get on and off.

parts.ex: The cakes in the shop window look amazing.
parts.def: The big window at the front of a shop, where things are shown.

parts.ex: We stood under the awning until the rain stopped.
parts.def: A piece of cloth over a shop window, to keep off the sun and rain.

parts.ex: The chemist's has a green cross on its sign.
parts.def: A board with a name or a picture on it.

parts.ex: The shop door is open.
parts.def: The part you open to go into a building.

parts.ex: Is there a cash machine near here?
parts.def: A machine in a wall where you get money with your bank card.

parts.ex: Can you put this letter in the post box?
parts.def: A red box in the street where you post letters.

parts.ex: I'll meet you by the lamp post.
parts.def: A tall post in the street with a light at the top.

parts.ex: Put your rubbish in the bin.
parts.def: A container in the street for rubbish.

parts.ex: Let's sit under the parasol.
parts.def: A big umbrella over a table, to keep off the sun.

parts.ex: There's a free table outside the café.
parts.def: A piece of furniture with a flat top on legs.

parts.ex: The menu board says soup of the day is tomato.
parts.def: A small board outside a café with the food and prices.

parts.ex: There's a tree in front of the clothes shop.
parts.def: A tall plant with a trunk, branches and leaves.

parts.ex: We waited in the bus shelter out of the rain.
parts.def: A small building with a roof at a bus stop.

parts.ex: Check the timetable - the next bus is at ten past.
parts.def: A list of the times when buses come.

parts.ex: An old man is sitting on the bench.
parts.def: A long seat for two or more people.

parts.ex: Walk on the pavement, not in the road!
parts.def: The path at the side of a road for people to walk on.

parts.ex: People live in the flats above the shops.
parts.def: Homes on one floor of a bigger building.

parts.ex: There's a round window in the roof.
parts.def: The top cover of a building.

parts.ex: Smoke is coming out of the chimney.
parts.def: A pipe on a roof that takes smoke away.

parts.ex: All the windows of the bank are closed.
parts.def: Openings in a wall with glass.

parts.ex: Always cross at the zebra crossing.
parts.def: Black and white lines across a road where people can cross.

parts.ex: The beacons flash so drivers see the crossing.
parts.def: A yellow light on a black and white pole that shows a zebra crossing (in Britain).

parts.ex: Look both ways before you cross the road.
parts.def: A hard way for cars to drive on.

parts.ex: A red car is driving along the high street.
parts.def: A road vehicle with four wheels and an engine.

parts.ex: I ride my bike to the shops.
parts.def: A bicycle: two wheels that you ride.

parts.ex: The cyclist is wearing a helmet.
parts.def: A person riding a bike.

parts.ex: Always wear a helmet on your bike.
parts.def: A hard hat that protects your head.

parts.ex: The high street is full of shoppers on Saturday.
parts.def: A person who is shopping.

parts.ex: Cars must stop for pedestrians at the crossing.
parts.def: A person who is walking in the street.

parts.ex: Take an umbrella - it might rain.
parts.def: A thing you hold over your head when it rains.
